evidence.clarity: 1440 and 390: “Wake to thirty minutes of sunrise. One dial, no app” identifies the bedside product and the one control; the CTA names reservation.
evidence.fit: The page states the $20 is refundable, says no card is taken because checkout is not connected, and avoids a firm shipment date or sleep claim.
evidence.distinctiveness: The dark-bedroom illustration, one-dial simulation and cream prototype section give the page a recognisable bedside-light language.
evidence.proof: The animated room scene and range control show off, ember and full brightness; its caption says the colour rise is drawn, not measured.
evidence.craft: 1440: high-contrast cream serif type on navy, copper action buttons and a parchment prototype section create clear visual hierarchy; at 390 the CTA remains prominent.
evidence.mobile: At 390 the phone menu opens, the promise and reserve CTA remain readable, and the illustration/dial stack vertically; the more detailed prototype explanation is below the fold.
evidence.honesty: The page says the CAD drawing is not the final shape, the colors are illustrative and checkout opens email without taking a card; the destination address itself is not in the brief.
evidence.interaction: At all widths, dragging the range from -30 to 0 changes the readout from Off to Full brightness; Play pauses/resumes and the mobile Menu toggles.
evidence.copy: “Set it once before bed” and “The lamp’s real brightness will be specified before the first batch” distinguish the intended experience from prototype evidence.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: the scene and controls sit with the promise and CTA. At 390 the action is visible and the drawing begins, but the dial/readout needs scrolling.

problems: The final reserve action uses an email address not provided in the brief, so visitors cannot be sure the displayed placeholder can accept their request.
The interactive lamp scene and dial are lower on the phone than the headline, so the wake-up experience is not fully demonstrated in the first viewport.
The long bottom-half prototype and FAQ sections make the reservation terms require a substantial scroll.

hard_fail_flags.evidence: The repeated “Reserve a Morrow” action ultimately opens `mailto:reserve@morrow.example`, an address that the client brief does not supply.
hard_fail_flags.steps: At 390 or 1440, click the hero “Reserve a Morrow” anchor, then click the button in the reserve section. It resolves to `mailto:reserve@morrow.example`; the X08 brief provides no reservation email address.

evidence.clarity: 1440: “A lamp that wakes you the way a window does” is followed by the thirty-minute dawn description and the “Reserve a place” action.
evidence.fit: The page explains deposits are not open, no payment is due today, the $20 is refundable, and the housing design is still unsettled.
evidence.distinctiveness: The bedroom illustration, working dial and light progression are specific to this product; the label says drawn, not photographed.
evidence.proof: The custom dial changes time and room brightness; End reaches 7:00/full light and Home returns to 6:30/dark, and Play animates the rise.
evidence.craft: 1440: a restrained night palette transitions to warm dawn and a cream planning section; at 390 the oversized scene pushes the controls and CTA down.
evidence.mobile: 390 has no overflow, but the full nav stays visible and the large illustration plus text pushes the reserve control below the first screen.
evidence.honesty: The page accurately says deposits are not open, but a valid form claims “Your place is held” and promises emails while saving only to localStorage.
evidence.interaction: At 1440, 768 and 390, the dial responds to keyboard Home/End and Play/Pause works; empty/bad email errors, valid submit confirms, and “wrong address” clears it.
evidence.copy: “Hardware runs late” and “we are not going to print a month we might miss” address the buyer’s shipping concern; no sleep-science or review claims appear.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: the promise, drawn room and dial are visible; at 390 the reserve action is not in the first screen and the email form is much farther down.

problems: The local-only confirmation says the visitor is held in line and promises future emails, though the data never leaves the browser.
At 390 the hero has no visible reserve CTA before the large illustration and dial; the main conversion path is several screens down.
The headline is evocative but does not say “bedside wake-up lamp” until the lede.

hard_fail_flags.evidence: After a valid email, the page announces “Your place is held” and promises future emails, but the script only writes the value to localStorage; `HOLD_ENDPOINT` is empty and no request or backend receives it.
hard_fail_flags.steps: Open B/index.html, scroll to Reserve, submit a valid email, then inspect the confirmation and `localStorage.morrow.held`. The form hides and promises future mail while no network submission occurs; reload in a fresh browser context and the place is gone.

reason: A balances the warm bedroom drawing, touchable light ramp and reservation terms in a clearer phone composition. B’s hand-drawn scene is also effective, but its reservation control is pushed below the mobile opening and its confirmation is not honest; I would reconsider if the form disclosed local-only storage and the action moved higher.
